item.text: {"chapter_id":"7B","shard_id":"7B-S03","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E010","BATCH-0030-E002","BATCH-0030-E003","BATCH-0030-E012","BATCH-0031-E010","BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0031-E015","BATCH-0040-E004","BATCH-0041-E008","BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0042-E009","BATCH-0042-E010","BATCH-0043-E006","BATCH-0043-E009","BATCH-0043-E011","BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0044-E012","BATCH-0045-E010","BATCH-0046-E004","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0046-E010","BATCH-0047-E007","BATCH-0047-E008","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0047-E011","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0049-E002","BATCH-0050-E007","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0051-E007","BATCH-0051-E008","BATCH-0051-E010","BATCH-0055-E007"],"answers":[{"question_id":"7B.1","answer":"The shard contains repeated adverse evidence concerning factual claims, denial of surveillance, attacks on critics, and institutional representations, but also qualifying evidence of correction or acknowledgment. Verificado classified 13 of 30 factual claims in the 2022 Fourth Government Report as false and 8 as misleading, and classified 10 of 25 2022 morning-conference claims as false and 6 as misleading; the supplied material does not establish knowing intent or later correction. López Obrador denied Pegasus surveillance and said no such contracts existed, while leaked records reportedly showed a 2019 contract and surveillance cases; he characterized the activity as intelligence rather than espionage. The Supreme Court later found that the National Guard reform transferred operational and administrative control to Defense, while the executive materials denied an intent to militarize or establish authoritarianism; the Court did not determine subjective deception. He publicly acknowledged leaked reports about his health as true and apologized after prematurely disclosing a Banxico rate decision. His statements during the Otis response accused critics of exaggerating casualties, while AP reported substantial unmet needs; the early figures were still evolving.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0042-E009","BATCH-0043-E009","BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0046-E004","BATCH-0047-E007","BATCH-0047-E008","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0055-E007","BATCH-0048-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0055-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most fact-check evidence concerns 2022 rather than 2023.","Several adverse claims are allegations, leaked-record reports, or commentary rather than final findings of deliberate deception.","The shard does not provide a comprehensive record of corrections or sworn testimony."]},{"question_id":"7B.2","answer":"The shard records limited corrective or cooperative conduct alongside substantial evidence of denial, minimization, or failure to remedy. López Obrador acknowledged his health conditions after leaked disclosures and apologized for the premature Banxico disclosure. Conversely, he denied or minimized reported Pegasus surveillance, criticized journalists and organizations reporting it, and reportedly did not correct disputed information according to a quoted media editor. The shard also reports that the government defended military nondisclosure in Ayotzinapa, that the GIEI left after lack of cooperation, that INAI was paralyzed after appointments were vetoed or rejected, and that a substantially similar secrecy order followed a Supreme Court invalidation. No final remedies are supplied for several investigations.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0047-E007","BATCH-0047-E008","BATCH-0030-E012","BATCH-0031-E010","BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0051-E007","BATCH-0051-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0051-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not establish the president's personal knowledge of every institutional failure.","Several misconduct matters remained investigations or allegations, without final legal outcomes, recovery, or sanctions.","The reported correction pattern is not comprehensive."]},{"question_id":"7B.3","answer":"The shard reports potential family conflicts and unresolved safeguards rather than a final adjudicated conflict-of-interest finding. MCCI reported that relatives and friends of López Obrador's sons held federal posts and that he had not introduced legislation regulating potential conflicts involving himself and his family. In March 2023 he said he was certain there was no conflict concerning his son José Ramón, while ordering an investigation or response and directing that the matter be included in a Pemex report. Opposition allegations described nepotism and conflicts, but were explicitly partisan allegations. The material does not establish a final finding, recusal, divestment, or personal enrichment.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0040-E004","BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0049-E002","BATCH-0050-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0049-E002","BATCH-0050-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied final investigation or judicial finding resolves the alleged family conflicts.","The shard does not document recusal, divestment, or a complete disclosure record.","Some allegations come from opposition or opinion sources."]},{"question_id":"7B.4","answer":"The shard documents allegations and institutional risk concerning associates, family networks, military contracts, and public procurement, but does not establish personal or family profit from office through a final finding. Reports described alleged contracts involving associates of López Obrador's sons, relatives in government, and corruption risks including direct awards, ghost or penalized businesses, shell companies, and weak procurement transparency. Segalmex investigations involved alleged diversion and more than 10 billion pesos not accounted for; its director, an old friend appointed by López Obrador, was removed but reassigned to another government post. The material does not prove López Obrador's personal enrichment or complete recovery and accountability.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0040-E004","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0049-E002","BATCH-0050-E007","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0049-E002","BATCH-0050-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No final adjudication establishes personal presidential or family profit.","Close-associate and institutional misconduct is not automatically attributable to the ruler.","Recovery, sanctions, and final outcomes are largely absent."]},{"question_id":"7B.5","answer":"The shard contains evidence of personalized and loyalty-oriented staffing and delegation, mixed with insufficient evidence to assess general competence. A scholarly biography describes reliance on a small circle of confidants and personal judgment. Segalmex's director was described as an old friend of López Obrador and was reassigned after corruption investigations rather than leaving public service. The military was expanded into major civilian functions after civilian bureaucrats were dismissed, with analysts describing the armed forces as a disciplined and loyal substitute and reporting partisan alignment. These records support concerns about loyalty and politicized appointments, but do not establish that every appointment was made for self-dealing or that appointees lacked competence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E003","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0055-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0055-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard lacks a comprehensive appointment-by-appointment competence and process record.","Military dependency partly predated López Obrador.","Some causal interpretations are expert commentary rather than formal findings."]},{"question_id":"7B.6","answer":"The shard contains substantial adverse evidence that independent scrutiny was weakened or obstructed, alongside some surviving independent checks. Reports describe military surveillance of journalists and a human-rights defender, refusal to provide Ayotzinapa records, alleged interference with investigations, public attacks on the Supreme Court and critics, paralysis of INAI after appointments were blocked, and repeated efforts to eliminate or subordinate independent oversight bodies. The Supreme Court invalidated the National Guard transfer and a national-security order, and Amnesty records some positive international accountability commitments, but implementation remained incomplete. Personal presidential direction is clear for several institutional choices and public attacks, while direct presidential knowledge of particular military operations is not established.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E012","BATCH-0031-E010","BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0042-E010","BATCH-0043-E006","BATCH-0045-E010","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0051-E007","BATCH-0051-E008","BATCH-0051-E010","BATCH-0055-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0041-E008","BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0051-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence varies from court findings to advocacy assessments and opinion commentary.","The shard does not establish personal presidential authorization for each surveillance or military obstruction episode.","Some institutional weaknesses and military autonomy predated the target period."]},{"question_id":"7B.7","answer":"The shard reports repeated noncompliance, secrecy, or pressure affecting accountability mechanisms. Examples include refusal to provide Ayotzinapa interception records, defense of military nondisclosure, failure to implement or accept judicial constraints concerning National Guard control, a near-identical secrecy order after Supreme Court invalidation, paralysis of INAI after presidential vetoes and coalition action, and denial of Pegasus operations despite reported contracts and infections. There are also contrary or qualifying records: Banxico remained institutionally independent after presidential pressure, the Supreme Court issued adverse rulings, and Mexico formally accepted some international accountability mechanisms. No comprehensive record of subpoenas or personal judicial compliance is supplied.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E012","BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0043-E006","BATCH-0045-E010","BATCH-0047-E007","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0051-E007","BATCH-0051-E010","BATCH-0048-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0051-E010","BATCH-0044-E008"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not establish a complete record of subpoenas, audits, pardons, or personal judicial compliance.","Some evidence describes institutional or military conduct rather than direct presidential action.","Several allegations lack final judicial resolution."]},{"question_id":"7B.8","answer":"The shard shows both formal commitments and apparent reversals or contested good faith. López Obrador promised that journalists and activists would not be spied on, while subsequent reporting described Pegasus-related contracts and surveillance during his administration; he denied that this was espionage. He previously opposed militarization but later expanded military control, and the Supreme Court found that the National Guard reform transferred control to Defense despite executive language denying militarization or authoritarian intent. His economic and social claims emphasized favorable distributional outcomes while fact-checkers found numerous false or misleading claims and reporting supplied contrary poverty and distribution data. These materials show contested consistency but do not prove that every policy change was for personal advantage.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0047-E007","BATCH-0055-E007","BATCH-0046-E004","BATCH-0042-E009","BATCH-0043-E009","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0031-E013"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0046-E004","BATCH-0055-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a complete promise-to-implementation ledger.","Policy reversal may reflect changed circumstances rather than deception.","Personal advantage or concealed tradeoffs are not established for every cited reversal."]},{"question_id":"7B.9","answer":"The shard reports potential favoritism and clientelism involving family associates, political networks, universal programs, military institutions, and privileged access, but attribution and motive are mixed. MCCI and opposition sources described relatives, friends, and associates of the president's sons receiving posts or contracts; AP reported that social-program design shifted benefits toward less-poor groups and quoted criticism that universal pensions could be politically attractive because seniors vote, while also reporting genuine beneficiaries and poverty reductions. Military expansion created new portfolios and revenues for generals close to the president. Segalmex involved an old friend appointed to lead the agency and alleged direct awards to connected companies. These are material concerns, but several claims remain allegations or institutional patterns rather than findings of personal direction.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0040-E004","BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0031-E015","BATCH-0049-E002","BATCH-0050-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E015","BATCH-0042-E001","BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0049-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No final procurement or corruption finding links López Obrador personally to the alleged benefits.","The shard does not establish that social-program targeting was designed primarily for electoral reward.","Associate misconduct and countrywide procurement risk require explicit attribution, which is incomplete here."]},{"question_id":"7B.10","answer":"The shard presents a mixed but predominantly adverse integrity environment. Positive or qualifying evidence includes austerity and modest-lifestyle claims, public acknowledgment of leaked health information, an apology for the Banxico disclosure, some international accountability commitments, and continued judicial or central-bank independence despite pressure. Adverse evidence includes repeated stigmatizing attacks on journalists and civil-society critics, alleged failure to correct disputed claims, resistance to transparency institutions, military secrecy and impunity concerns, family-conflict allegations, and weakened independent scrutiny. The evidence supports concern that presidential rhetoric and institutional choices normalized hostility toward scrutiny, but broad violence, corruption, and repression are not automatically personal dishonesty or corruption.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E003","BATCH-0029-E010","BATCH-0031-E010","BATCH-0031-E011","BATCH-0043-E011","BATCH-0044-E012","BATCH-0047-E008","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0051-E007","BATCH-0051-E008","BATCH-0051-E010","BATCH-0046-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E003","BATCH-0044-E008","BATCH-0048-E003","BATCH-0051-E010","BATCH-0046-E008"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard contains no systematic public-trust survey or complete record of ethical reforms.","Some adverse material is advocacy, partisan, or opinion commentary.","The evidence does not establish that all national violence or corruption was personally caused or directed by López Obrador."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["This output is limited to shard 7B-S03 and makes no score or cross-ruler comparison.","The supplied records vary substantially in period fit; several concern 2022 or earlier background rather than 2023-only conduct.","Allegations, leaked records, advocacy assessments, and opinion commentary must not be treated as equivalent to final legal findings.","Country-level corruption, violence, press-safety, and institutional conditions are included only where the supplied material identifies a ruler-specific statement, decision, benefit, protection, tolerance, concealment, or response."]}
